gaps.sentence: She was two hours late, ___ annoyed the interviewer.
gaps.hint: comment on the whole situation before the comma
gaps.explanation: When a clause comments on the whole previous statement, use 'which' after the comma.

gaps.sentence: The company's shares, ___ rose sharply yesterday, are still undervalued.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to the shares; 'that' is impossible in a clause set off by commas.

gaps.sentence: The author ___ books sell millions worldwide lives in Iceland.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' links the author to her books; 'who' could not be followed directly by 'books'.

gaps.sentence: The Eiffel Tower, ___ attracts millions of visitors, was completed in 1889.
gaps.explanation: For things in non-defining clauses use 'which'; 'that' is not allowed after a comma.

gaps.sentence: The manager, for ___ the team played so hard, thanked everyone.
gaps.hint: played for the manager — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: The preposition 'for' demands the object form 'whom' for a person.

gaps.sentence: The 1990s was the decade ___ mobile phones became common.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'in which' after time nouns; 'which' cannot stand alone here.

gaps.sentence: Everything ___ he said turned out to be true.
The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.
